rationale: The latest race data confirms that the current candidate performs very well on the oval and s-bend tracks but still fails to complete the slalom track, going off track early with high rms error and steering oscillation. The slalom track's sharp turns require even more precise and stable control. The feedback and race data suggest that the robot is still too fast and exhibits excessive steering oscillation in the slalom. To address this, I will reduce the base_speed further from 1.0 to 0.9 to improve stability and reduce overshoot in tight curves. Additionally, I will soften the PID gains by lowering kp from 6 to 5 and kd from 2 to 1.5 to reduce steering oscillations. I will increase ki from 1.0 to 1.5 to enhance steady-state error correction, aiming to improve line tracking precision on curves. The geometry and sensor layout remain unchanged as they have proven stable and well balanced. I continue to request the full set of observations to monitor performance comprehensively. I expect these changes to improve slalom completion and reduce steering oscillations while maintaining strong performance on other tracks.
